Manevychi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. About 30 Jewish families lived in Manevychi in the early 20th century, growing to 462 (57 percent) by 1921; Neskhizh, Stolin-Karlin, and Stepan Hasidic streams were present, along with three synagogues, one led by Rabbi Josef Gordon. In July 1937, the victory of a local Jewish football team, HaShmonai, triggered a pogrom. By the Wehrmacht's occupation, the Jewish population exceeded 550, including Polish refugees; during the first Aktion on August 26, 1941, 327 were shot. A ghetto created September 2, 1942, was liquidated three days later; 200 Jews escaped, some joining the partisan detachment Kruk, before all remaining residents were murdered. This cemetery, founded in the early 20th century, was completely demolished by Soviet authorities, with the location of its tombstones unknown today.
